ebw-jss1-01-001.png: A 10x10 grid of 100 small squares with a single top-left square shaded, showing one hundredth (1/100, 0.01) - one part out of one hundred.
ebw-jss1-01-002.png: A 10x10 grid of 100 squares with four squares (top of the first column) shaded, showing four hundredths (4/100, 0.04).
ebw-jss1-01-003.png: A 10x10 grid of 100 squares with the whole first column (10 squares) shaded, showing ten hundredths = one tenth (10/100 = 1/10, 0.1).
ebw-jss1-01-004.png: A 10x10 number chart counting from 10,000 to 1,000,000; each cell rises by 10,000 across a row and by 100,000 down a column - counting to one million in ten-thousands and hundred-thousands.
ebw-jss1-01-005.png: A 10x10 number chart counting from 990,100 to 1,000,000 in steps of 100 across a row and 1,000 down a column - the final stretch up to one million.
ebw-jss1-01-006.png: A 10x10 number chart counting from 999,901 to 1,000,000 in steps of 1 across a row and 10 down a column - the last hundred numbers before one million.
ebw-jss1-01-007.png: A 10x10 number chart counting from 10,000,000 to 1,000,000,000; each cell rises by 10,000,000 (ten million) across a row and by 100,000,000 (hundred million) down a column - counting to one billion in ten-millions and hundred-millions.
ebw-jss1-01-008.png: A 10x10 number chart counting from 999,990,100 to 1,000,000,000 in steps of 100 across a row and 1,000 down a column - the final stretch up to one billion.
ebw-jss1-02-001.png: A 1-100 hundred-square (numbers 1 to 100 in a 10x10 grid) with the prime numbers shaded blue (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, ... 97) - a chart highlighting all primes up to 100.
ebw-jss1-04-001.png: A circle drawn as an orange sliced into 8 equal segments, slightly separated - a whole divided into eighths.
ebw-jss1-04-002.png: A circle (orange) of 8 equal segments with 6 shaded orange and 2 left white - representing six-eighths (6/8 = 3/4).
ebw-jss1-04-012.png: Two whole green apples and one half-apple (cut to show the core) - illustrating two and a half (2 1/2), a mixed number.
ebw-jss1-04-013.png: Five apple-halves (each cut to show the core) - showing five halves (5/2), the same quantity as two and a half as an improper fraction.
ebw-jss1-04-014.png: A rule diagram for converting the mixed number 3 3/5 to an improper fraction: a blue 'x' arrow multiplies the whole number 3 by the denominator 5, and a red '+' arrow adds the numerator 3.
ebw-jss1-04-015.png: Three equal bars showing equivalent fractions: 1/2 (one of two parts shaded), 2/4 (two of four), and 4/8 (four of eight) - all equal to one half.
ebw-jss1-04-016.png: Ten apple-halves (four in the top row, six in the bottom) - showing ten halves (10/2 = 5).
ebw-jss1-04-017.png: Two bars each divided into eighths: the top shows 6/8 (six parts shaded) and the bottom shows 4/8 (four parts shaded).
ebw-jss1-04-020.png: A 10x10 hundred grid with 21 squares shaded (the first two columns plus one more) - showing 21/100 (0.21).
ebw-jss1-04-021.png: A 10x10 hundred grid with red lines grouping it into 5 equal horizontal bands of 20 squares - showing fifths (each band = 1/5 = 20/100).
ebw-jss1-04-022.png: A 10x10 hundred grid grouped into 5 bands with the bottom 2 bands shaded red - showing two-fifths (2/5 = 40/100 = 0.4).
ebw-jss1-05-001.png: A horizontal number line from -6 to 6 with a dot at each integer and 0 in the middle, labelled 'negative numbers' to the left and 'positive numbers' to the right.
ebw-jss1-05-002.png: Two crocodile drawings as a greater-than/less-than mnemonic: the open mouth faces the larger number - left shows 6 > 2, right shows 2 < 6.
ebw-jss1-05-003.png: A number line from -10 to 10 with a dot at every integer - an integer number line including negatives, zero and positives.
ebw-jss1-05-008.png: A -10 to 10 number line showing a jump of 6 units in the positive direction from 1 to 7, illustrating 1 + 6 = 7.
ebw-jss1-05-009.png: A number line showing a jump of 7 units in the positive direction from -6 to 1, illustrating -6 + 7 = 1.
ebw-jss1-05-010.png: A number line showing a jump of 9 units in the negative direction from 4 to -5, illustrating 4 - 9 = -5.
ebw-jss1-05-011.png: A number line showing a jump of 6 units in the negative direction from -2 to -8, illustrating -2 - 6 = -8.
ebw-jss1-06-001.png: A circle divided into 4 equal quarters, none shaded - an empty fourths fraction circle.
ebw-jss1-06-002.png: A circle in 4 quarters with one quarter shaded red - one quarter (1/4).
ebw-jss1-06-003.png: A circle in 4 quarters with the top two quarters shaded red - two quarters (2/4).
ebw-jss1-06-004.png: Two circles with an equals sign: the left is 2/4 (two of four quarters shaded), the right is 1/2 (top half shaded) - showing 2/4 = 1/2.
ebw-jss1-06-005.png: A circle in 4 quarters with one quarter shaded purple - one quarter (1/4).
ebw-jss1-06-006.png: Two circles with an equals sign: the left is 2/4 (purple), the right is 1/2 (purple) - showing 2/4 = 1/2.
ebw-jss1-06-007.png: A circle divided into 10 equal segments, none shaded - an empty tenths fraction circle.
ebw-jss1-06-008.png: A circle in 10 segments with 7 shaded orange and 3 white - seven tenths (7/10).
ebw-jss1-06-009.png: A circle in 10 segments with 8 shaded orange and 2 white - eight tenths (8/10).
ebw-jss1-06-020.png: Two circles in quarters: the left fully shaded red (4/4, one whole) and the right with one quarter shaded (1/4).
ebw-jss1-06-021.png: A circle divided into 5 equal segments with the top two shaded teal - two-fifths (2/5).
ebw-jss1-06-022.png: Three identical circles each divided into fifths with two-fifths shaded teal - three copies of 2/5.
ebw-jss1-06-023.png: Three circles in fifths showing a sequence: the left fully shaded (5/5), the middle with one-fifth shaded (1/5), the right empty (0/5).
ebw-jss1-06-024.png: A circle in 4 quarters with three shaded yellow - three quarters (3/4).
ebw-jss1-06-025.png: A circle with each quarter subdivided into three (twelfths), 9 segments shaded yellow and 3 white - showing 3/4 = 9/12.
ebw-jss1-06-026.png: A circle divided into twelfths with 9 segments shaded and the bottom-right quarter (3 twelfths) white - nine twelfths (9/12 = 3/4).
ebw-jss1-06-027.png: A circle divided into 5 segments with the top two shaded teal - two-fifths (2/5).
ebw-jss1-06-028.png: A circle of fifths subdivided into tenths (yellow guide lines) with two-fifths (= four tenths) shaded teal - showing 2/5 = 4/10.
ebw-jss1-06-029.png: A circle divided into 10 segments with four shaded (teal and green) - four tenths (4/10 = 2/5).
ebw-jss1-06-030.png: Four empty circles each divided into 3 equal parts (thirds), none shaded.
ebw-jss1-06-031.png: Four circles each divided into thirds, with each third filled a different colour - whole circles partitioned into thirds.
ebw-jss1-06-032.png: A circle divided into 8 segments with six shaded yellow and the bottom-right quarter (two-eighths) white - six-eighths (6/8 = 3/4).
ebw-jss1-06-033.png: A circle in 8 segments with six shaded yellow (segments numbered 1,2,...) and two white - six-eighths (6/8), illustrating counting in eighths.
ebw-jss1-06-034.png: A circle divided into 8 segments, six filled with different colours and the bottom-right two left white - six-eighths shown as a colour wheel.
ebw-jss1-06-035.png: A circle in 4 quarters with the top-right quarter shaded red - one quarter (1/4).
ebw-jss1-06-036.png: A circle in 4 quarters with three shaded purple - three quarters (3/4).
ebw-jss1-06-037.png: A circle in 4 quarters with the top half (two quarters) shaded purple - two quarters (2/4 = 1/2).
ebw-jss1-10-001.png: A labelled diagram of the algebraic expression 3x + 5y - 9: 'coefficients' point to 3 and 5, 'variables' point to x and y, 'constant' points to 9, and 'terms' lists 3x, 5y, 9.
sv-g10-math-lit-12-gd-0001.png: A circular flow diagram of the data-handling cycle: Develop research question, Plan research, Collect data, Classify and organise data, Summarise/represent/analyse data, looping back to the research question.
sv-g10-math-lit-12-gd-0003.png: A diagram titled 'Methods of data collection' branching to four methods with icons: Observation (globe and magnifying glass), Interview (two people at a table), Questionnaire (a checklist clipboard), and Database (a database icon).
